Robustness rebuild · comprehensive edition · for discussion

Nested confounder ladder, spec curve, and Oster bounds are in

A rerun of the DER-equity regressions on the real analysis sample (2,549 CA ZIP/ZCTAs, filtered to a frozen common sample of 1,150–1,160 rows per outcome) implementing REGRESSION_ROBUSTNESS_PLAN.md in full: a genuinely nested ladder (C1–C5, plus a saturated model S and an over-controlled lower bound O) replaces the mislabeled M1–M8 chain; a 48-specification curve stress-tests every income/race coefficient; Oster (2019) δ bounds quantify how much unobserved selection would be needed to explain each effect away. main already has this ladder running for two outcomes (PV, storage) - the new work lives entirely in a separate notebook (notebooks/regression_robustness_ladder.ipynb) that extends it to all ten without touching a single file main already has. This version is meant to be read without the repo open.

1 · Methodology

What changed, and why it's credible now

The paper's regressions were previously presented as an "increasingly rigorous" model ladder, but the code did not implement one — each specification varied exactly one control block relative to a fixed baseline (siblings), rather than accumulating controls (rungs). M3 swapped the climate control instead of adding to it; M6 dropped climate for geography instead of building on M5. This rebuild keeps that sibling fan — it is genuinely useful for asking which single block moves a coefficient — but adds a second, actually-nested structure alongside it.

The seven new models

C1Core: income, race, poverty, climate
→
C2+ education, housing value
→
C3+ housing structure, tenure
→
C4+ utility FE
→
C5 = S+ county FE, county-clustered SEs (climate dropped)
→
O+ demand, infrastructure (mediators)
Confounders vs. mediators
C1–C5 use only pre-treatment confounders (education, housing, tenure, utility/county FE). Electricity demand and infrastructure capacity sit on the causal path from income/race to DER adoption — conditioning on them estimates a direct effect, not the total effect the paper reports. They're held out of the saturated model and only enter Model O, which is deliberately framed as a conservative lower bound, never the headline number.
Frozen common sample
All seven models are fit on one intersected, listwise-deleted sample per outcome (common_sample_index), including the county min-cluster-size filter. Coefficient movement across rungs therefore reflects added controls only, not a shrinking or shifting sample — verified: every rung reports identical N for every outcome.
Specification curve
Every subset of the six confounder blocks, fit on the raw (unstandardized) scale, reporting the four focal terms. 26 = 64 combinations, minus the 16 that stack both county FE and utility FE (near-collinear, near-exhaustive partitions of the same ZIPs) → 48 valid specifications per outcome. outputs/tables/spec_curve.csv — 1,920 rows (48 × 10 × 4)
Oster (2019) δ
How much selection on unobservables, relative to the observed confounders, would be needed to drive a coefficient to zero. Compares Model C1 (restricted) to Model S (full), with Rmax = min(1.3 × R²full, 1). δ ≥ 1 is the conventional "robust" threshold — the omitted-variable bias would have to exceed the observed selection. δ = βfull(R²full − R²restr) / [(βrestr − βfull)(Rmax − R²full)]

Full C1→C5 progression, headline outcomes

R² climbs monotonically for every outcome as controls accumulate — the largest single jump is always county FE (C4→C5). Model O (mediators added on top of C5) pushes R² further still, e.g. PV 0.492→0.658, storage 0.422→0.658 — see the diagnostics table in §5 for every outcome's full R² path.

Aggregate EV charging is fragile on race terms (0/48 on % Black, despite the baseline table reporting it as significant) while DC fast chargers alone are comparatively robust on income (29/48) — the charger-subtype decomposition story the paper already tells is visible directly in this table now.

Flag for discussion

PV and aggregate charging's δ are uninterpretable in the usual sense, and that's itself a finding. Oster's formula assumes controls shrink a coefficient toward zero; for PV's income term (and charging's), the full confounder set increases the effect instead (PV: 0.43→0.47 raw scale). The formula still returns a number (−32.5, +26.0) but it doesn't mean "this many times the observed selection would explain the effect away" — it means the assumption underlying δ doesn't hold there. Storage is the clean case: δ = 0.96 on income, meaning selection on unobservables just under the scale of the observed confounders would zero out the effect — a legitimately reportable bound. Several race terms clear δ ≥ 1 outright (storage % Hispanic 1.99, PV % Asian 1.57, storage % Asian 1.29) and are safe to cite directly. Recommend: report δ where the sign behaves as expected, and reframe PV/charging's non-attenuation as its own qualitative result rather than forcing every cell through the δ framework.

Flag for discussion

Model O has one real collinearity problem, but it doesn't touch the headline terms. For the eight non-wind outcomes, Model O's infrastructure-mediator block includes both wind_capacity_mw and wind_turbine_count as controls — two measures of essentially the same thing, VIF ≈ 12.2 against each other. That inflates the standard errors on those two coefficients specifically; it does not touch income or race, whose VIF stays under 8 in Model O for every outcome (table above). Not a problem for the ladder's headline claims, but if Model O's infrastructure coefficients themselves ever get quoted, they need this caveat or the two wind terms should be combined/dropped first. (The two wind outcomes, y_wind_mw and any_turbines, correctly exclude these controls already — they'd be circular there — and their Model O max VIF is a clean 7.8.)

6 · For discussion

Open items before this goes back into the draft

  • The Word draft (site/index.docx) still has the old figures and "eight-model ladder" language.Nothing in the manuscript text has been touched — only the underlying tables/figures and the code that produces them. Methods section, Figure 4/12 captions, and the "staged model ladder" framing all need a rewrite pass once the framing below is settled.
  • PV's non-attenuating income effect deserves its own paragraph, not a footnote.It's the most surprising result in this rebuild and doesn't fit the Oster δ framework cleanly (§4) — probably belongs in Discussion as a distinct finding about non-price barriers rather than folded into the robustness appendix.
  • Report Model O (over-controlled) in the main text or push it to appendix-only?It's explicitly a conservative lower bound (adds demand + infrastructure, which sit on the causal path) — useful context but easy to over-read as "the" preferred number if it's too prominent.
  • 48 of 64 spec-curve combinations, not the full 64.Combinations stacking county FE and utility FE together are dropped as near-collinear. Worth a one-line footnote on the SI figure, or we loosen the exclusion if you'd rather see the other 16.
  • Aggregate EV charging's fragile race coefficients (0/48 on % Black) versus the baseline table's significant result, and DC-fast's comparative robustness on income (29/48).Consistent with the paper's existing point that aggregate charging masks charger-type composition — now directly quantifiable. Worth cross-referencing the spec curve numbers in that section.
